definition: a thick sauce made from tomatoes, vinegar and sugar
hook: There was no tomato in ketchup. There was fish.
modernAnchor: A red squeeze bottle, a paper cup of fries, a diner table. We call it ketchup.
journey: In Hokkien-speaking ports, ke-tsiap named the salty liquid drawn off fermented fish. Dark, sharp and nothing like a condiment for chips.
English and Dutch traders met it in Southeast Asia in the 1600s and carried the word home along with a taste for the stuff.
British cooks had no fermented fish to hand, so they rebuilt it from what they did have: mushrooms, walnuts, oysters, anchovies. Mushroom ketchup outsold every rival for a century.
Tomatoes arrived late, in America in the 1800s, and won so completely that the word now means only them.
